segments.name: fetch_url
segments.text:
Understanding Hydration in Sourdough

Hydration is the ratio of water to flour in a dough, by weight. A dough with 500 g flour and 375 g water has 75% hydration. Higher hydration gives a more open crumb but is harder to shape. Beginners often do best between 65% and 70%. Whole wheat flour absorbs more water than white flour, so you can raise hydration by a few percent when using it. Temperature matters too: a warmer dough ferments faster and feels slacker.
